title: Run kickoff and record hardware and availability
outcome: Confirm the team accounts, development and training resources, and weekly availability.
acceptance: Record OS, CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM for available machines without private identifiers.
Confirm the workstream ownership and weekly availability.
Confirm the team start date, official deadline, and university report requirements.

title: Reproduce the environment on all team machines
outcome: Make the same foundation service and checks runnable by every member.
acceptance: Run uv sync --frozen on the available team machines.
Post sanitized doctor and pytest results.
Record and resolve operating-system-specific setup problems.

title: Review related work and candidate data sources
outcome: Identify relevant primary studies and usable data sources.
acceptance: Prepare a reading table with links, methods, metrics, and limitations.
Identify comparisons that fit the available resources.
Record candidate datasets and their licenses.

title: Benchmark candidate models on the demonstration machine
outcome: Select a model candidate using measurements.
acceptance: Measure latency, memory use, and small task examples for suitable candidates.
Record license, exact revision, and hardware.
Recommend a model and input limit with supporting results.

title: Run a small LoRA feasibility experiment
outcome: Verify that a small adapter can be trained, saved, reloaded, and resumed.
acceptance: Pin a training environment compatible with the actual GPU.
Smoke-test the training script on the GPU.
Save and reload an adapter; record time and memory and a fallback if training is infeasible.

title: Agree on Python scope and supported refactoring types
outcome: Select one bounded Python refactoring type and state what is outside the three-week release.
acceptance: Prepare before/after examples and reference tests for each task.
Update the proposal and requirements.
Set measured input, retry, and resource limits.

title: Supervisor review: scope and feasibility
outcome: Present the proposal and feasibility evidence and agree on the scope.
acceptance: Prepare a short summary, experiment links, and specific questions.
Record supervisor feedback, agreed decisions, and pending questions.
Create follow-up Issues and update the plan.

title: Curate a licensed sample dataset
outcome: Prepare task-appropriate examples with a provenance manifest.
acceptance: Record source, license, inclusion criteria, and exclusion criteria.
Review a sample for valid code and behavior-preserving changes.
Estimate a feasible dataset size from evidence.

title: Split data and check leakage and duplicates
outcome: Produce reproducible splits separated by source.
acceptance: Create train, validation, and test splits by source_group.
Check exact and near-duplicates and record curation decisions.
Save hashes and a split manifest and freeze the test set.

title: Implement and measure the single-role baseline
outcome: Record baseline outputs from the original model.
acceptance: Provide an inference script with fixed settings, error records, and timing.
Use an initial task rubric and reference tests.
Do not use the test set to tune prompts.

title: Freeze the comparison protocol and numerical targets
outcome: Separate model adaptation, role coordination, and resource effects.
acceptance: Define groups A/B/C/D and their resource budgets.
Specify measures, denominators, and timeout handling.
Record targets after the baseline and before final test evaluation.

title: Specify API and role contracts and run states
outcome: Agree on schemas before parallel implementation.
acceptance: Document requests, results, errors, and run-state transitions.
Record the workflow and storage decisions.
Add example JSON and contract tests.

title: Supervisor review: data and baseline
outcome: Review data quality, baseline results, and planned comparisons.
acceptance: Present samples, licensing, split checks, and baseline results.
Review targets and the evaluation method.
Record decisions and follow-up Issues.

title: Implement a replaceable local model provider
outcome: Use one interface for the original model and adapted model.
acceptance: Load a pinned model revision.
Bound generation and return clear timeout and inference errors.
Verify that an adapter can replace the baseline without changing the API contract.

title: Implement structured analysis-role outputs
outcome: Analyze the agreed task types using the shared schema.
acceptance: Return valid JSON with the finding type, location, and supporting reason.
Cover invalid code and code with no supported finding.
Enforce a documented inference-call limit.

title: Implement bounded refactoring proposals
outcome: Generate a proposed change and reason without executing it.
acceptance: Return code, a reason, and task type, or an explicit failure.
Use the agreed task, context, and input limits.
Test syntax failures and schema-invalid model outputs.

title: Implement run API and state records
outcome: Expose traceable runs and clear failure handling.
acceptance: Implement the agreed contracts and failure states.
Record settings, model revisions, and stage durations.
Use a clearly identified fake provider for GPU-independent integration tests.

title: Build the initial code-input and result interface
outcome: Connect one usable input-to-result interaction to the service.
acceptance: Show input, waiting, result, and failure states.
Present a readable diff and explanation.
Document local frontend setup and operation.

title: Run and record the first fine-tuning experiment
outcome: Save a reloadable adapter and validation results.
acceptance: Use only train records for updates and validation records for selection.
Record settings, manifests, and a training dependency lock.
Save the adapter and checksum and compare with the baseline on validation data.

title: Demonstrate an early end-to-end case
outcome: Show one complete case from input to result.
acceptance: Run the interface, API, and model together.
Show original and proposed code with the available check results.
Record incomplete review features explicitly.

title: Supervisor review: integration and first training run
outcome: Present the complete path and initial training comparison.
acceptance: Show a demonstration and actual experiment settings and results.
Explain observed failures and resource constraints.
Record decisions and next-phase priorities.

title: Implement review and role coordination
outcome: Coordinate the roles with bounded correction attempts.
acceptance: Keep the agent verdict separate from deterministic check results.
Use a bounded correction path and an explicit stop reason.
Test timeouts and failures in each role.

title: Design and verify a separate runner for trusted examples
outcome: Run reference tests outside the API with reviewed isolation controls.
acceptance: Exclude network, secrets, host access, and the Docker socket.
Enforce time, memory, CPU, and process-cleanup limits.
Complete the runner safety checklist and isolation tests before enabling execution.

title: Integrate verification and failure results into the interface
outcome: Present evidence without a misleading success state.
acceptance: Show syntax, tests, and review as separate results.
Handle missing reference tests explicitly.
Verify model and runner failures without modifying original input.

title: Select and integrate the model using validation data
outcome: Use a justified candidate rather than automatically using the latest run.
acceptance: Record the selection rule and validation evidence.
Retain the original model if adaptation does not help, with an explanation.
Update the model card and artifact reference.

title: Verify first-release acceptance criteria
outcome: Trace agreed P0 behavior to test evidence.
acceptance: Provide a requirement, test, and result matrix.
Cover errors, input limits, and timeouts.
Verify diff, download, and preservation of the original input.

title: Supervisor review: integrated first release
outcome: Review acceptance examples and freeze core features.
acceptance: Show the acceptance demonstration and remaining defects.
Review limitations and the final evaluation plan.
Record decisions and repair Issues.

title: Run the independent final evaluation
outcome: Evaluate groups A/B/C/D on the frozen test set.
acceptance: Retain every attempt, including failures and timeouts.
Measure latency and resource use alongside quality.
Assess a sample with the fixed rubric and explain ambiguous cases and failure patterns.

title: Verify clean setup and fix critical defects
outcome: Reproduce the release from clean setup instructions.
acceptance: Complete a clean-clone installation in a fresh environment; prefer a second machine, and explicitly record whether different hardware was actually tested.
Fix critical defects without tuning on the test set.
Update setup instructions and measured hardware limits.

title: Write the academic report and update the guides
outcome: Prepare a report grounded in actual work and results.
acceptance: Cover the problem, related work, method, design, implementation, experiments, and limitations.
Trace reported figures and numbers to retained evidence.
Update the developer guide, user guide, and model card.

title: Prepare the presentation and repeatable demonstration
outcome: Prepare a team presentation and backup recording.
acceptance: Use a stable demonstration with a success and failure example.
Agree on speaking roles and rehearse questions.
Store a small permitted backup recording in the GitHub release within quota.

title: Publish the initial delivery release
outcome: Publish an identifiable release and its supporting materials.
acceptance: Create a tag, release notes, and artifact checksums.
Respect model/data licenses and storage limits.
Complete the delivery checklist and link the report and demonstration.

title: Supervisor review: initial delivery and next priorities
outcome: Record delivery feedback and prioritize subsequent development.
acceptance: Present the release, findings, and limitations.
Record the supervisor review.
Prioritize follow-up work without assuming a larger scope.
